title: Macramé beaded wall hanging
subtitle: A square-knotted panel with wooden beads threaded onto the filler cords
excerpt: A macramé wall hanging with large wooden beads threaded onto the filler cords between sections of square-knot sennit. The beads add weight and visual rhythm to the piece. The finished hanging is about 40 cm wide and 60 cm long plus fringe.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from standard macramé craft practice. Beaded macramé wall hangings are a staple of intermediate macramé workshops; the square-knotted panel with threaded bead accents is a common teaching project.

glossaryTerms.definition: A flat symmetrical knot made with two working cords around two or more filler cords. The most used knot in decorative macramé work.
A chain of repeated knots, usually square knots or half-hitches, worked vertically to create a column of knotting.
The mounting knot used to attach cords to a dowel or ring at the start of a macramé piece.

. The beads slide onto the filler cords between knot groups; the working cords knot below the bead to hold it in place. Mount the cords on a wooden dowel with
. Use 5 mm single-strand or 3-ply cotton cord in natural or dyed colour; the cord must pass through the bead holes without forcing.

items.name: 5 mm cotton macramé cord, natural or dyed
items.qty: about 40 m for a 40 cm wide by 60 cm hanging

items.name: Large wooden beads (hole diameter at least 6 mm to accept the cord)
S-hook or nail for hanging the work board

content.text: Cut 16 cords, each 2.5 m long. Fold each cord in half and attach with a lark's head knot to the dowel, working across the full 40 cm width. The 16 cords produce 32 working ends. Push the lark's head knots close together along the dowel until the row is even.

Divide the cords into groups of four. Work a square knot with each group: outer two cords are the working cords, inner two are the fillers. Work across the full width to produce eight square knots. Leave a gap of 2 cm below the knots before the next row.

On each group of four cords, thread a bead onto the two filler cords (the inner cords of each group). Slide the bead up to rest against the bottom of the square knot. Work a second square knot immediately below the bead to hold it in place. Continue alternating square-knot sennit with threaded beads at intervals of your choosing down the length of the hanging.

Offset the cord groupings for the second and third rows: shift by two cords so each square knot uses cords from two adjacent first-row groups. This alternating pattern produces the classic macramé diamond lattice. Thread beads at alternating row positions for a scattered bead effect, or at every row for a denser beaded surface.

After the last row of knotting, cut the remaining cord ends to a uniform length for the fringe. Trim the fringe to a straight horizontal line, or cut at an angle or in a V-shape for a more decorative finish. Unravel the cord ends slightly to soften the fringe. Attach a hanging cord to each end of the dowel.

items.problem: The beads do not stay in position and slide down past the lower square knot
items.cause: The bead hole is larger than the cord diameter, so the cord can pass back through the bead after knotting
items.fix: Choose beads whose hole diameter closely matches the cord diameter. If using beads with large holes, work two or three square knots below the bead rather than one.

items.problem: The knotted panel is pulling to one side and not lying flat
items.cause: The square knots are being tied more tightly on one side than the other, or the cords are not being kept even across the width
items.fix: Pin the work to the macramé board as you go and check the alignment after every row. Keep the square knots at the same tension throughout.
